name: "Freezer Friendly" Indian Red Lentil Dahl with Cilantro (Batch-Cooking)

instructions.primary_message: This recipe makes about 16 cups of dahl or 8 (2-cup) servings.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 (3 inch) piece ginger root
1 small bunch cilantro
1 lemon

instructions.primary_message: Quarter chili peppers lengthwise; seed and remove ribs with a spoon to reduce spice level. Mince and place in a medium bowl. (Be careful with chilis; do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.)
Peel, halve, and small dice onions. Add to the bowl with the chili pepper.
Preheat a large pot over medium heat.
Once the pot is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add chili pepper, onion, and salt; cook, stirring occasionally, until golden and very soft, about 10 minutes.
instructions.secondary_message:
2 tbsp neutral vegetable oil
½ tsp salt

instructions.primary_message: Meanwhile, peel and mince ginger and garlic.
Using a strainer, rinse lentils under cold water; drain and set aside.
When the onion is golden, add ginger, garlic, and spices to the pot. Cook, stirring occasionally, until fragrant, about 2 minutes.
instructions.secondary_message:
2 tbsp garam masala
4 tsp cumin, ground
4 tsp paprika
2 tsp salt
1 ½ tsp turmeric, ground
¾ tsp black pepper
½ tsp cayenne pepper

instructions.primary_message: Add drained lentils, broth, tomatoes, coconut milk, and water, to the pot; stir to combine the dahl and bring to a boil over high heat. Once boiling, reduce to a simmer and cook, stirring occasionally, until lentils are tender and dahl has thickened, 20-25 minutes. (If a looser dahl is preferred, add 1-2 cups additional water towards the end of cooking and adjust seasoning as desired.)
instructions.secondary_message:
8 cups vegetable broth
2 (411 g) can diced tomatoes
380 ml coconut milk
1 cup water

instructions.primary_message: Meanwhile, shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves.
When the dahl is done, juice lemon into the pot. Add cilantro, stir to combine, and remove from heat. Set aside to cool to room temperature, stirring occasionally, about 30 minutes.
Once the dahl has cooled to room temperature, divide between containers.

STORING: Cover each container with an air-tight lid (or wrap tightly with plastic wrap). Place in the freezer for up to 3 months. HEATING: For best results, thaw dahl in the fridge overnight. Warm in a saucepan set over medium-high heat, stirring occasionally, until heated through, 4-5 minutes.
CHEF'S NOTE: Serve dahl alongside rice or naan bread, topped with yogurt and more fresh cilantro if desired!
